title: nml --json row, formatVersion 1
$comment: The `$defs/revision` const is THIS FILE's revision, stated once (the `contract` row's and the `summary` row's `revision` reference it): a stream written at another revision fails validation on its first row, before any finding. Every addition to this file (a key, a row type, an enumerated value) moves the const by one, with one CHANGELOG entry (`--json formatVersion F, revision R`) naming the additions; scripts/docs_test.py holds the const to the writer's (`nml version --json`, row one), refuses a shape change at an unchanged revision (docs/json/nml-ndjson-v1.shape.txt is the generated shape record) and a revision without one. A rename, a removal, a type change or a narrowed vocabulary moves `$defs/formatVersion` and this file's name.
description: One line of the line-delimited JSON every nml verb writes to stdout under --json: a `type`-discriminated object. This document IS the wire contract for formatVersion 1 (docs/stability.md), at the revision the `contract` row names: a field may be added to a row without bumping the version (the revision moves); renaming or removing one, or narrowing a vocabulary, must bump the version. Every row is closed (`additionalProperties: false`): a consumer validates strictly only against the schema at the revision the stream's FIRST row (`contract`) names, and otherwise ignores keys it does not know. The `contract` row opens every run and the closing `summary` row carries the same `formatVersion`, `revision` and `nmlVersion`. Columns (`col`, `endCol`) are 1-based BYTE columns of the line as the run read it. scripts/docs_test.py validates every executed transcript's rows against this file and that every stream opens with `contract` and closes with `summary`.

formatVersion.description: The contract's number — THIS FILE's, stated once: moved by a rename, a removal, a type change or a narrowed vocabulary, never by an addition, and with it this file's name.

revision.description: The additions axis within the format — THIS FILE's revision, stated once (the `contract` and `summary` rows reference it): every addition moves it by one, with one CHANGELOG entry naming the additions. The writer (`nml-cli/src/out.rs` REVISION) is the source; scripts/docs_test.py holds this const, the generated shape record and the CHANGELOG ledger to it.

contract.description: The stream's FIRST row, on every path that emits a row at all: the format's number, its revision (the additions axis; this file's own revision, as a const) and the binary that wrote the stream. The closing `summary` row repeats the three.

code.description: A stable diagnostic code, or null for an uncoded finding.

verb.description: The verb the run executed, as typed.

closure.description: The kernel's word on the whole universe: every manifest enumerated and loaded (`complete`), the walk cut short (`truncated`), or a live input that failed to load (`unloadable`).

skipReason.description: Why the walk left an entry out of its enumeration, by policy. `unkeyableName`: the entry's name is no key (not UTF-8, or bearing a path separator) — its row's `key` is the holding directory's and `entry` carries the name. `componentBound`: a directory at the 64-component bound, never listed.

related.description: A secondary location that explains the primary one, in its own file.

cause.description: The finding whose refusal a row reports, on a row that wraps another finding under a code of its own — NML2088 over a manifest's first finding (a repeated entry NML2093, a repeated declaration NML1000, an unknown property NML2001, a parse finding, a rule of the loader's own NML2094–NML2104), NML2091 over a declared source's first finding: its code (never null — a codeless finding hides no fact the row does not state, and a row reported under the inner finding's own code, NML2081, wraps nothing), its sentence, and its place in its own file (`line`/`col` null when the finding has no place or its file could not be read). One level: the innermost finding, the one to act on. Absent from every other row, so a consumer reads `cause?.code ?? code`.

edit.description: One byte-exact edit of a suggestion, resolved against the file as this run read it: the text from `line`:`col` up to `endLine`:`endCol` (1-based; columns are BYTE columns of the line; the end exclusive; equal for an insertion) is replaced by `lines` joined with a newline. Every element is one line and never hosts a control character, so a consumer prints or applies a line as a line.

suggestion.description: A machine-applicable edit set the finding carries (rustc's structured suggestion) in the file `source` names — the finding's own, or another (NML2064's `layers:` grant goes in the manifest that lacks it). `kind` is the exclusivity: `didYouMean` a singular correction, `fix` one of several mutually exclusive alternatives (never auto-applied while siblings exist), `delete` a structural removal, `insert` a block added as the last entry of a named block. Every kind is exact by construction (the kernel never guesses); only edits the run resolved are here, at least one `edits` entry each, and a consumer applying them later first verifies the file is as the run read it (rerun `nml check`). `nml fix` applies a finding's edits to the file it was given only.

diagnostic.description: One finding. `source` is the workspace KEY of the file it is in (the path as typed for a workspace-free verb); `line`/`col` are 1-based (`col` a byte column) and null for a locationless finding (a universe note, a kernel rejection, a fixer's own note); `suggestions` are its machine-applicable edits, resolved (empty when it carries none); `cause` rides only a row that reports another finding's refusal (revision 2).

error.description: A failure line. `kind` says what failed: the invocation itself (`usage`, exit 2), one target of a many-target run that continued (`target`), or the run's closing verdict when no `result`/`summary` row carries it (`run`).

result.description: One target's verdict — always the last row for that target. `declarations` is null for `validate` (symbols only).

root.description: The workspace root the run resolved in: the canonical path, how it was fixed, the fence entry's kind when derived within a VCS fence, and the entry above the fence that shadows the derived universe (another `.git`, or a root marker above a directory fence).

truncatedUnit.description: A budget unit the walk stopped inside: every file under `unit` is denied while the rest of the universe stands.

skipped.description: What the walk left out of its enumeration by policy: `byWhy` the EXACT count per reason; `rows` the first `--max-findings` entries by depth then key (`0` lifts the bound); `hidden` how many rows that budget held back.

entry.description: The entry's own name where `key` cannot carry it (`unkeyableName`), spelled lossily.

withheld.description: What the finding-PRINTING budget held back (`--max-findings`); the counts on the row stay exact. `byCode` keys are codes, or `(uncoded)`.

summary.description: The run's ONE closing row, emitted last on every path — a clean run, a failing one, a parse error, an absent target, a usage error. It carries the `contract` row's three facts again. `exit` is the process's own exit code. The universe fields are null for a verb with no universe. `fix` carries its own counters in the same row, on every path — `routed` among them: the distinct edits its findings carry that lie in another file, refused and pending there. `schemaSources` is how many schema sources a `--schema <dir>` invocation contributed, null when none was given: `0` says the directory held none, so every target was validated against its own definitions alone.

claimant.description: A binding that claims the file: its package, the claim's class, the manifest it came from, the anchor directory and the `files` glob that matched.

governingBinding.description: The claimant that governs the file, with the step that selected it.

layers.description: The composition grant: `granted` alone when composition is denied or the open context permits it; the grant's own fields when a binding carries one.

binding.description: `nml binding`'s answer for one file: the key, whether the file is absent (the binding shown is what WOULD govern the path), the root and universe facts the `summary` carries too, the governing verdict, the binding or the claimants, the grant, and the notes (diagnostic rows; under `--quiet` the errors among them).

fix.description: One file `nml fix` changed (or, dry-run, would change): `diff` is the unified diff on a dry run, else null; `routed` the distinct edits standing in this file's findings that lie in ANOTHER file (refused here, applied there — an operator's change pending in a manifest), a part of `remaining`.

parse.description: `nml parse`'s AST as data (its shape is the AST's own, not this contract's).

explain.description: One diagnostic code's summary and full document (`--list` emits one row per code).

version.description: `nml version --json`: the binary's version (the `contract` and `summary` rows carry the same string as `nmlVersion`).

limit.description: One published bound (`published: true`, with its value and classification), or one bound the census deliberately does not publish (`published: false`, with the reason in `what`).
